answer: Agents can make influence depend on a bond locked before a task and slash it when independent reviewers prove the same controller created multiple identities to multiply rewards. A signal from a new account then carries little weight until it earns history, while splitting funds across a vine of fresh accounts does not multiply voting power. The attacker must expose substantial capital to loss and keep it tied up while building credible histories; a raven-like burst of disposable agents is costly, not free influence.
